deviations: D1 (IRealtimePublisher.DriverStatusChangedAsync signature changed): The original signature was DriverStatusChangedAsync(Guid driverId, DriverStatus status, CancellationToken ct). Added a required fleetId: DriverStatusChangedAsync(Guid driverId, Guid fleetId, DriverStatus status, CancellationToken ct). This enables SignalRRealtimePublisher to route to the correct fleet:{fleetId}:dispatch group. Updated callers: GoOnlineEndpoint (passes driver.FleetId), GoOfflineEndpoint (passes driver.FleetId), OrderService (passes order.FleetId), NoOpRealtimePublisher, RecordingRealtimePublisher.

D2 (Hub-scope tenant injection): TenantResolutionMiddleware only runs on the SignalR negotiate HTTP request, not on hub method invocations. FleetHub takes CurrentTenant (concrete class, same assembly) as a constructor parameter and calls SetTenantFromClaims() at the start of each hub method that queries the DB. Customer Subscribe uses IgnoreQueryFilters() with explicit ownership predicate (CustomerUserId == sub) because customer JWTs carry no fleet_id claim — this is tenant-safe by construction.

D3 (Active order resolution — simple query per broadcast): On each accepted UpdatePosition, FleetHub queries the DB for the driver's active order (Status in Accepted/Arrived/InProgress). This is one extra async DB call per accepted position update. Chosen over caching for simplicity; the WI explicitly sanctioned this approach. Can be cached in a future optimization.

D4 (DB flush in FleetHub using IServiceScopeFactory): The WI described 'track lastDbFlush per driver in the store; write via scoped DbContext from IServiceScopeFactory'. Implemented: DriverPositionStore tracks lastDbFlush per driver entry. When flush is due, FleetHub.FlushPositionToDatabaseAsync creates a new DI scope, fetches the Driver with IgnoreQueryFilters(), updates LastLat/Lng/PositionAt, and saves. Flush errors are swallowed (Warning log) so position broadcasts continue.

D5 (First update always flushes): lastDbFlush is initialized to DateTimeOffset.MinValue. The first accepted update always triggers a DB flush (so Driver.LastPositionAt is immediately written, not 30s stale for a fresh connection).

D6 (DriverPositionChanged from FleetHub — no fleetId on IRealtimePublisher path): FleetHub.UpdatePosition broadcasts DriverPositionChanged directly via Clients.Group (dispatch group + order group) without going through IRealtimePublisher. The IRealtimePublisher.DriverPositionChangedAsync method exists for external callers (background jobs); it can only broadcast to driver:{driverId} without fleetId context.

D7 (Non-driver UpdatePosition — silent ignore): Non-driver callers (dispatchers, customers) invoking UpdatePosition receive no error, no exception — the call is silently swallowed with a Debug log. This avoids leaking role information via error responses.

D8 (Non-owner Subscribe — silent ignore): Non-owner customers invoking Subscribe receive no error — the call is silently swallowed with a Debug log. This avoids leaking order existence information to unauthorized callers.

D9 (TaxiApiFactory.FakeTimeProvider exposed): FakeTimeProvider is now created in the TaxiApiFactory constructor (not ConfigureWebHost) and exposed as a public FakeTime property. ConfigureWebHost registers the pre-created instance. FleetHubTests creates its own TaxiApiFactory per test class to advance time freely without contaminating the shared PostgresFixture.Factory instance.

D10 (SignalR transport — Long Polling): Tests use HttpTransportType.LongPolling with factory.Server.CreateHandler() because the TestServer does not support WebSockets. AccessTokenProvider is used (not query string) since Long Polling sends Authorization headers directly. The query-string path in Program.cs OnMessageReceived remains in place for production browser WebSocket connections.

D11 (AuthHelpers.MintTokenFor added): A public static MintTokenFor(userId, role, fleetId, fleetSlug) helper was added to AuthHelpers so FleetHubTests can obtain raw token strings for SignalR connections without going through HTTP client extension methods.

D12 (OrderChangedDto): A hand-written record DTO (OrderChangedDto) is used for the OrderChanged SignalR event to avoid EF navigation cycle serialization issues when sending the Order entity directly over SignalR. Contains: Id, FleetId, PublicCode, Status, DriverId, CustomerUserId, UpdatedAt.
D13 (needs_library_research skipped): Environment facts state no subagents exist. Research was not dispatched; existing project patterns (SignalR already in stack) and prior-art code were sufficient.

D14 (DriverPositionStore lock-per-entry): Throttle check and state update are wrapped in a per-entry lock block to make TryUpdate thread-safe under concurrent invocations for the same driverId. ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd provides atomic construction.

D15 (NewOrderOffered payload shape): Fixed to match §10 contract — two separate arguments SendAsync('NewOrderOffered', dto, expiresAt, ct) so clients can register on('NewOrderOffered', (order, expiresAt) => ...) correctly. Original wrapped-object approach would have broken client deserialization.

D16 (TimeProvider in FleetHub): Replaced DateTimeOffset.UtcNow with timeProvider.GetUtcNow() per rules/csharp-style.md#timeprovider. The at value goes into DriverPositionChanged payload and Driver.LastPositionAt flush — using the injected clock ensures test determinism and correct behavior with FakeTimeProvider.
notes: Throttle design: DriverPositionStore.TryUpdate checks (now - lastAccepted >= 3s). FirstOrDefault is avoided — per-entry lock prevents races. FakeTimeProvider.Advance(3s) advances the injected clock so the second batch of updates crosses the threshold, proving both the throttle and the clock injection. Flush design: first accepted update always flushes (lastDbFlush == MinValue), subsequent flushes occur every 30s per driver. Active-order resolution: simple DB query per accepted broadcast (no cache); WI sanctioned this. Subscribe refusal: silent (no error), documented. Non-driver UpdatePosition: silent (no error), documented. FakeTimeProvider: exposed on TaxiApiFactory; FleetHubTests creates its own factory per class.
